previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, morbid obesity, and a history of venous thrombosis was admitted for evaluation of persistent nausea and malaise. She had no abdominal pain or vomiting but reported a dry cough and night sweats. Initial concerns for infection led to a brief course of antibiotics, but imaging showed a chronic retrocardiac opacity unlikely to be infectious, and antibiotics were discontinued. Nausea was thought to be related to gastroesophageal reflux, and she was started on omeprazole. A sacral fungal rash with a fissure was identified and treated with topical ketoconazole. She remained stable, her symptoms improved, and she was discharged to extended care with plans for ongoing dialysis and outpatient follow-up for a breast mass, dermatology, and primary care. Her home medications, including warfarin, insulin, and constipation regimens, were continued.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  ULTRASOUND GUIDED WIRE LOCALIZATION, RIGHT BREAST

INDICATION:  Two suspicious masses in the right breast. The patient was
referred for a preoperative wire localization prior to surgical resection.

PROCEDURE:  The procedure, risks, and benefits were discussed with the patient
and written informed consent was obtained.  The patient's medications were
reviewed.  A pre-procedure time-out was performed using three patient
identifiers.

Using standard aseptic technique, and ___ cc of 1% Lidocaine for local
anesthesia, a localizing needle and subsequently a wire were placed through
each lesion under ultrasound guidance. The targets are both located at the
proximal stiffeners.

UNILATERAL DIGITAL POST-PROCEDURE MAMMOGRAM, RIGHT: Post procedure mammogram
shows two new localizing wires in the right breast. The targets are located at
the proximal stiffeners of the wires.
The lesions are located in the inferior central and outer right breast.

The patient tolerated the procedure well. There were no immediate
complications.

The procedure was performed by Dr. ___ and the attending
radiologist, Dr. ___.

IMPRESSION:
